customManagers.description: Swift releases. swiftlang/swift tags them swift-X.Y.Z-RELEASE. Version and commit are captured by ONE regex so Renovate moves them together -- the builds fetch GitHub's tarball of SWIFT_SHA (shipyard's fetch_pinned_source.sh), verified by SWIFT_TARBALL_SHA256, which the pins bot writes on the PR's branch; so the commit, not the tag, is what is built, and a version bumped without its commit would build the old source.

The swiftlang/llvm-project commit the build support is cut from. llvm-project tags every Swift release swift-X.Y.Z-RELEASE, exactly as swiftlang/swift does, so this tracks that tag the same way: version and commit in ONE regex. The version is LLVM_SWIFT_RELEASE rather than SWIFT_VERSION only because two managers capturing the same literal would both rewrite it; build-llvm.sh fails unless the two are equal and LLVM_SHA is the commit at the tag.

swift-cmark, the compiler's Markdown parser, tagged swift-X.Y.Z-RELEASE per Swift release like llvm-project and tracked the same way: version and commit in ONE regex. build-toolchain.sh runs check_release_pin on it.

mavericks-clang-22's cross toolchain, the C/C++ compiler of the 10.9-hosted Swift toolchain. The whole pin is the version: fetch-clang22.sh verifies the pkg against that release's own SHA256SUMS. The versioning regex reads -mavericks.N as the build number; Renovate's default would coerce it away and never propose a repackage.

Recaulk, whose librecaulk.a supplies the few post-10.9 APIs build.sh's RECAULK_RUNTIME_SYMBOLS names, linked statically into libswiftCore. The whole pin is the version: fetch-recaulk.sh verifies the pkg against that release's own SHA256SUMS. Recaulk tags YYYYMMDD.N; the versioning regex reads N as the build, so two releases on one day order.

packageRules.description: ONE PR per Swift release, moving the Swift pin, the llvm-project pin and the swift-cmark pin together. Apart, each fails its release-pin check (build-llvm.sh, build-toolchain.sh), so none could merge. The builds fetch each commit as GitHub's tarball, verified by a SHA-256 in pins.env that Renovate cannot compute: .github/workflows/pins-bot.yml writes those on the PR's branch, pushing as the pins-bot GitHub App so that release.yml runs on its commit (gitIgnoredAuthors keeps that commit from marking the branch as edited), so a patch bump still automerges on green.
prBodyNotes: **The tarball pins:** `.github/workflows/pins-bot.yml` writes `LLVM_TARBALL_SHA256`, `SWIFT_TARBALL_SHA256` and `CMARK_TARBALL_SHA256` on this branch, after checking that each tarball is its commit's tree, and runs `release.yml` on its commit; that run's `build` is the check this PR merges on. Until then CI fails at the first fetch, naming the pin. If the bot failed, run `sh scripts/pin-source-tarballs.sh` on this branch and push `pins.env` (INGREDIENTS.md).
